title: Tech Architect: MERN | SaaS | AWS/Azure
description: Role: Tech Architect: MERN | SaaS | AWS/Azure Multi-Tenant SaaS Platform: MVP to General Availability Role Summary The Tech Architect owns the technical design of the SaaS platform and its path from a working MVP to a live, production product. The role decides the architecture, sets engineering standards, writes and reviews critical code, and holds the team to them. It is accountable for the platform’s structure, not for running every workstream: specialist roles (data, AI/ML, DevOps, security, QA) implement within the architecture this role defines. Key Responsibilities Multi-tenant architecture: Design the tenant model, tenant isolation, rate limiting and quotas, horizontal scaling and cost model; choose between monolith, modular monolith and microservices. API and service design: Define versioned REST/GraphQL APIs , service boundaries, event-driven patterns ( Kafka/RabbitMQ ) and data models across MongoDB, SQL and Redis . MVP to production: Decide what to reuse vs. re-architect; set production standards (error handling, logging, monitoring, tests, performance); own readiness reviews, load testing, go-live, rollback and post-launch support. MERN leadership: Lead MongoDB , Express , React and Node.js development; set front-end and back-end standards; write and review production code. Cloud architecture: Define the AWS/Azure target architecture, deployment topology and CI/CD approach (blue-green/canary, Docker, Kubernetes); DevOps/SRE implements infrastructure as code and observability. Identity and extensibility architecture: Design per-tenant SSO (SAML 2.0, OIDC/OAuth2, SCIM), RBAC, public APIs, webhooks, SDKs and a versioned, sandboxed plugin model. Security architecture: Set defense-in-depth design (gateway, WAF, authN/Z, encryption, secrets, audit logs); lead threat modelling and design reviews. The Security Specialist runs testing, compliance and vulnerability management. AI-assisted engineering: Introduce agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude Code) with review standards, guardrails and CI quality gates for AI-generated code. Technical leadership: Approve high-level designs, guide low-level designs, maintain architecture decision records and documentation, mentor senior engineers, run proofs of concept, and partner with product on trade-offs. Required Qualifications 10–15 years in software engineering, including 3+ years as an architect. Strong hands-on MERN; AWS or Azure; Docker, Kubernetes and CI/CD. Proven track record taking an MVP/POC to a live, production SaaS product. Multi-tenant SaaS, subscription billing, distributed systems and microservices; Kafka/RabbitMQ, SQL/NoSQL, Redis, object storage. SSO and enterprise authentication; security architecture (OWASP Top 10, secrets management, tenant isolation). Demonstrable use of agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude Code); LLM basics (RAG, tool calling). Awareness of SOC 2, ISO 27001 and GDPR; clear communication; experience leading architecture reviews. Preferred / Added Advantage Developer ecosystem or marketplace design; zero-trust, mTLS, SAST/DAST, SIEM; usage-based billing; MCP and LLM agents; Terraform/CloudFormation; SRE practices; cloud, TOGAF or security certifications. Pay: ₹2,500,000.00 - ₹3,500,000.00 per year Work Location: In person

title: Team Lead, Builder Developer III
description: ECI is rebuilding how software gets built: small teams of AI-first engineers, called Builders, who direct AI agents to design, ship, test and operate features end to end, measured in hours and days rather than sprints. As a Builder Manager, you lead that shift for an ECI India product team. You are not a ticket dispatcher or a status collector. You build the team, set the bar, and stay close enough to the code and the AI agents to know when the output is right and when it only looks right. WHAT IS A BUILDER AT ECI? At ECI, "Builder" is our title for engineers who work AI-first. Instead of writing every line by hand or working ticket by ticket, Builders direct AI agents to design, code, test and operate software, and are accountable for checking that the result is correct and safe in production. Builders work across Development, QA and Data. Builders work in pods: small, cross-functional teams (typically a handful of people) that own a product area end to end, from understanding the customer problem to running the feature in production. Builders grow along a four-level career framework. Levels reflect scope, independence and how much leverage someone gets from AI, not years of experience: Level 1: delivers well-defined work using AI tools, with coaching. Level 2: independently builds and runs AI agents and automated workflows for their features. Level 3 (Senior): sets technical direction for a product area; designs the testing, evaluation and safety checks that keep AI-built software reliable. Level 4 (Expert): shapes how AI-first engineering works across the whole organization. Every Builder is also assessed on five core competencies: Ownership, Delivery Reliability, Continuous Learning, Customer Orientation, and Communication & Collaboration. This role leads a team of Builders and is expected to operate at Level 3 or above. WHAT YOU WILL OWN 1. Product delivery, AI-first Own your product's engineering outcomes: what ships, at what quality, and how fast. Run delivery AI-first, in short cycles rather than two-week sprint rituals. Partner with product leadership to turn customer problems into well-scoped pieces of work with clear acceptance criteria and automated checks (evals) that prove the AI-built result is correct. Own production health: reliability, incident response, and DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, recovery time). 2. Build and grow the team Hire Builders at ECI's deliberately high bar, including a live, hands-on build exercise and assessment against the Builder career framework. Move an existing engineering team to the Builder way of working: assess each person against the framework, set clear development paths, and act decisively where someone isn't making the shift. Coach each person on the five core competencies, and grow Builders from one level to the next. Build the team's shared tooling and agent patterns, and lead across disciplines: Development, QA and Data Builders working as one team. De-risk the team's commitments, not just your own: spot fragile plans early and restructure them before they slip. 3. Engineering and AI standards Make AI the default in how the team builds, tests, documents and debugs, using tools such as Claude, Cursor and ECI's internal AI developer platform across the full lifecycle. Set the guardrails that keep speed safe: test coverage, code review of agent output, evals, feature flags and rollback. Govern AI systems in production with agent-level metrics alongside DORA: success and fallback rates, cost per task, retries, latency and user corrections. Keep agent behavior bounded through regression evals, versioning and human review. Modernize legacy code and workflows, treating them as a map of user intent to extract and automate. Keep AI usage measurable: attributed commits, Jira-linked work, and cost per outcome. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR Must have 10+ years in software engineering, including 3+ years leading engineering teams in a product company. Hands-on, current AI-first development experience: you direct AI agents in your own work, and can show what you built and how you verified it. Has built and run multi-agent workflows in production (e.g. LangGraph or similar) and designed evals for agents that change frequently. Credible technical depth to review agent-generated code and challenge architecture: modern web/SaaS stacks, APIs, SQL, CI/CD, cloud. [Add product stack specifics.] A track record of raising a team's bar: hiring well, coaching through change, and handling under-performance directly. Clear, evidenced strength in at least two of the five core competencies listed above. Delivery and production ownership: you have run releases, incidents and postmortems, and you manage with metrics. Clear communication with US product and leadership counterparts across time zones. Experience modernizing a legacy product while it continues to serve customers. Nice to have AI-driven test automation or synthetic test data generation at scale. Background in vertical SaaS or ERP software. How you work Player-coach: close enough to the work to grade it, without becoming the bottleneck. Rigor over hype: you know the difference between a compelling AI demo and production-grade software. Ownership: you close loops and never escalate without a recommendation. No surprises: you surface risk early and honestly.
